key.name: enabled
key.summary: Whether cell broadcast messages should be displayed
key.description: When this is disabled the shell will not show any cell broadcast messages, including important security warnings.

key.name: auto-brightness-offset
key.description: Fixed offset added to the calculated auto brightnes value.

key.name: status-icons
key.description: The list of currently enabled status-icon plugins.

key.name: favorites
key.summary: List of desktop file IDs for favorite applications
key.description: The applications corresponding to these identifiers will be displayed in the favorites panel along with running applications.

key.name: app-filter-mode
key.summary: How to filter apps in the overview. The default 'adaptive' shows only adaptive apps in mobile mode and all apps in docked mode. 'off' turns of all filtering.
key.description: Whether to filter out apps that aren't marked as adaptive in mobile mode.

key.name: force-adaptive
key.summary: List of desktop file IDs for applications that are adaptive for phone usage but not marked as such in their desktop file.
key.description: The applications corresponding to these identifiers will be displayed in the app grid panel even when in mobile mode that only lists touch capable apps that adapt to small screen sizes.

key.name: wwan-backend
key.summary: Which backend to use for interfacing with the cellular modem
key.description: The available backends are 'modemmanager' for ModemManager (the default) and 'ofono' for oFono. This setting is only read when Phosh starts, so a shell restart is required after changing it.

key.name: automatic-high-contrast
key.summary: Whether to switch to HighContrast theme in high brightness conditions
key.description: Setting this to true enables automatic switching to HighContrast on high ambient night levels.

key.name: automatic-high-contrast-threshold
key.summary: The light level (in Lux) to switch to HighContrast theme
key.description: When automatic high contrast is enabled this defines the light level at which to switch.

key.name: enable-suspend
key.summary: Whether to enable suspend from the power menu
key.description: Setting this to true allows manually suspending the device from the power menu. Suspend is an experimental feature on some devices and may result in crashes or instability.

key.name: quick-silent
key.summary: Allow to quickly silence the device
key.description: Setting this to true allows to set the phone to silent by pressing volume-down on incoming calls when the phone is locked. This feature is experimental.

key.name: shell-layout
key.summary: What information to use to layout UI elements.
key.description: This determines if Phosh will use device information to layout UI elements in order to not overlap with notches and cutouts.

key.name: osk-unfold-delay
key.summary: OSK unfold long press delay factor
key.description: Delay factor for long press on the home bar to unfold the keyboard. Valid values are [0.5,2.0]. Values less than 1.0 make the unfold trigger sooner, greater than 1.0 make the unfold trigger later.

key.name: enabled
key.description: When this is disabled the shell will not offer emergency call functionality.

key.name: shuffle-keypad
key.description: Setting this to true shuffle the digits on the PIN keypad to make eavesdropping harder.

key.name: require-unlock
key.description: Setting this to false allows unlocking without entering the PIN or password by simply swiping up.

key.name: wakeup-screen-triggers
key.summary: What notification properties wake up the screen
key.description: This setting defines what properties of a notification wake up the screen. (e.g. the notification's category or urgency).

key.name: wakeup-screen-categories
key.summary: Notification categories that wake up the screen
key.description: If matching by category is enabled defines which categories will wake up the screen.

key.name: wakeup-screen-urgency
key.summary: Notification urgency that wakes up the screen
key.description: If matching by urgency is enabled sets the lowest notification urgency that wakes up the screen.

key.name: lock-screen
key.description: The list of currently enabled plugins on the lock screen.

key.name: quick-settings
key.summary: List of enabled quick setting plugins
key.description: The list of currently enabled plugins on the quick settings box.

key.name: config
key.description:
Configuration for each monitor. The key is the monitor name and the value is a dictionary with the following keys: - 'scale': the scale factor for the monitor - 'x': the x position of the monitor - 'y': the y position of the monitor
NB: rotation is deliberately not stored so that we always start in the default orientation.

key.name: appid
key.description: Stores the application ID of the last app used or referenced by the shell. This can be used to restore session state or remember user preferences related to a specific app.

key.name: filtered-app-ids
key.description: List of application IDs to filter out and hide from the app list. Apps in this list will not appear in the launcher or app drawer.

key.name: screen-recorder-framerate
key.description: Frames per second to record at. 0 means let the compositor's own frame timing decide, which is the only setting that produces a file whose timestamps are true: a forced rate is stamped on the frames whatever rate they actually arrived at, so any difference between the two shows up as playback running fast or slow. The fixed rates are here for the cases where a constant-rate file is needed by something downstream.

key.name: screenshot-delay
key.description:
How long to wait between arming a screenshot from the quick settings and taking it. The wait is what makes the shot useful at all from there: the drawer has to be folded away first or it is the only thing in the picture.
Whatever was picked last is stored here and offered as the default next time, so the common case is two taps rather than a decision.

key.name: screen-recorder-speed
key.description:
How much faster than real time the finished recording plays. 1.0 is real time; 2.0 plays twice as fast.
This is applied after recording, by rescaling the timestamps and copying the streams through untouched, so it is exact and costs a fraction of a second whatever the length. Doing it instead by forcing a capture frame rate would only ever be approximate: the speed-up would be the ratio of the forced rate to the rate frames really arrived at, and that rate varies with what is on screen.

key.name: screen-recorder-codec
key.description:
The ffmpeg encoder to use. This device has no VAAPI -- the Mali G68 and the MediaTek encoder are both unusable through wf-recorder here -- so every workable choice is a software encoder and libx264 at a fast preset is the one measured to keep up with the display.
Settings offers libx264 and libvpx-vp9. libx265 is not offered: measured at 1078x2410 it encodes about five frames a second even at preset=ultrafast, so a recording made with it is a handful of frames.

key.name: screen-recorder-bitrate
key.description: Target bit rate, as an ffmpeg value such as '8M'. Empty lets the codec choose its own quality target, which for libx264 means constant quality rather than constant rate and generally gives a smaller file for the same picture.

key.name: screen-recorder-audio
key.description: Whether to record sound alongside the picture. Off records no audio at all rather than a silent track.

key.name: screen-recorder-audio-source
key.description: The PulseAudio/PipeWire source name to capture. A monitor source records what the phone is playing; an input source records the microphone. Empty uses the system default input. Ignored unless audio recording is on.

key.name: screen-recorder-touches
key.description: Draw a marker wherever the screen is touched, for as long as a recording is running, so that a recording explains itself. This is the compositor's own touch-point overlay, switched on when recording starts and off again when it stops.
